Run official CellOracle perturbation analysis

Source: R/RunCellOracle.R
RunCellOracle.Rd

Fit cluster-specific regulatory models and simulate gene perturbations using the unmodified CellOracle 0.20.0 Python implementation.

Usage

RunCellOracle(
  object,
  perturbation,
  group.by,
  base_grn = NULL,
  assay = "RNA",
  layer = "counts",
  features = NULL,
  reduction = NULL,
  stage_args = list(),
  model_dir = NULL,
  output_dir = NULL,
  store_expression = FALSE,
  tool_name = "CellOracle",
  envname = "celloracle_env",
  conda = "auto",
  docker_container = NULL,
  cores = 1L,
  seed = 1234L,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

A Seurat object with non-log RNA counts, clusters and a two-dimensional embedding. Perform cell/gene selection before calling this function.

perturbation

Named numeric vector of non-negative expression values. Zero simulates knockout. Multiple genes specify one joint perturbation.

group.by

Metadata column defining the clusters used for GRN fitting.

base_grn

Official TF-info data.frame with peak_id, gene_short_name and TF columns, a path to its parquet file, or a named list mapping target genes to character vectors of candidate TFs (the official TFdict format). Required for a new fit; do not pass SCOP TF/target/importance edge tables. No expression-derived GRN is generated automatically.

assay

Assay containing raw counts. Default is "RNA".

layer

Non-log count layer. Default is "counts". Fractional counts are accepted, matching the official raw-count import (including the official demo input). Log-transformed, scaled, integrated and SCT residual data should not be supplied; their provenance cannot be inferred from numeric values alone.

features

Genes to retain, in the requested order. NULL uses all genes in the assay. CellOracle recommends selecting approximately 1,000–3,000 genes before import; this wrapper does not silently select or normalize genes.

reduction

Reduction containing the two-dimensional embedding. NULL uses DefaultReduction(). The first two columns are used without recomputing.

stage_args

Named list of named argument lists for official methods: pca (perform_PCA), imputation (knn_imputation), links (get_links), filter (filter_links), fit (fit_GRN_for_simulation), simulation (simulate_shift), transition (estimate_transition_prob), embedding (calculate_embedding_shift), grid (calculate_p_mass), and mass_filter (calculate_mass_filter). Unspecified arguments retain upstream defaults. SCOP controls the perturbation, cluster-specific fitting, randomization reference, worker arguments and seed. In CellOracle 0.20.0, calculate_p_mass internally fixes smooth=0.8 and n_jobs=-1; the wrapper preserves that upstream behavior. Do not supply these two ineffective grid arguments. For small inputs explicitly choose suitable k, n_pca_dims, transition n_neighbors and grid n_neighbors; no silent clipping occurs.

model_dir

Directory containing model.celloracle.oracle and network.celloracle.links saved by a previous run. Reuse requires identical cells, genes, raw counts, cluster labels and embedding. Supply base_grn=NULL and no fitting-stage arguments when reusing a model.

output_dir

Optional new directory for official Oracle and Links HDF5 files. Existing directories are never overwritten. These files retain the full model and allow subsequent perturbations without refitting.

store_expression

Store cell-by-gene imputed_count, simulated_count and delta_X matrices in the returned object. Default FALSE limits size.

tool_name

Unused name for the result in object@tools. Existing entries are rejected; use a different name for another perturbation.

envname

Isolated environment prepared with PrepareEnv(modules = "celloracle"). Default "celloracle_env".

conda

Conda-compatible executable, passed to PrepareEnv().

docker_container

Optional name or ID of an already running Linux Docker container whose python has CellOracle 0.20.0 installed. This allows Windows R to use the same official runner without a local Python installation. SCOP transfers inputs/results through a temporary directory; envname and conda are unused. Model directories always refer to the R host. The function does not pull images, install packages or start containers.

cores

Positive worker count for official methods that honor it. The official grid routine may use all cores; see stage_args.

seed

Non-negative integer seed. NumPy and standard Python RNG states are restored on exit; the upstream transition routine also seeds Numba. Docker launches its child with PYTHONHASHSEED=seed to make upstream set-derived predictor ordering reproducible across processes. Local Python inherits its interpreter's hash seed; separate reference runs must use the same hash seed to compare bagging coefficients exactly.

verbose

Whether to display SCOP progress messages. Upstream diagnostic output and warnings remain visible. Docker output is also retained in the result's diagnostics character vector.

Value

A Seurat object with object@tools[[tool_name]] containing cell_shift (one row per input cell, with original coordinates, displacement and randomized displacement), grid_flow (official grid vectors, mass and exclusion mask), gene_effect (mean signed and mean absolute delta_X across cells), links and filtered_links (upstream edge tables per cluster), parameters, cells, genes, and optionally expression and model_dir. Expression matrices have input cell and selected gene dimnames. No live Python object is stored.

Details

Requires official celloracle==0.20.0, either in a Linux/macOS Python environment or in docker_container. Native Windows Python is not supported. Prepare the environment or container explicitly before analysis. The raw import performs CellOracle's own log transformation; no additional library-size normalization is introduced. PCA, imputation, network inference, edge filtering, coefficient fitting, simulation and projection all run in CellOracle. Network edge p-values are not perturbation-effect p-values. Results are predictions, not experimental knockout measurements.

References

Kamimoto et al. (2023). Dissecting cell identity via network inference and in silico gene perturbation. Nature. doi:10.1038/s41586-022-05688-9 .

See also

CellOraclePlot(), PrepareEnv()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# On Linux/macOS; prepare dependencies explicitly before analysis.
PrepareEnv(modules = "celloracle")
# On Windows use docker_container = "celloracle" with an already prepared,
# running Linux container instead of preparing local Python.
data(pancreas_sub)
pancreas_sub <- RunStandardWorkflow(pancreas_sub)
# Supply an official TF-info parquet prepared for the matching species.
pancreas_sub <- RunCellOracle(
  pancreas_sub, perturbation = c(Pdx1 = 0), group.by = "CellType",
  base_grn = "mouse_promoter_base_GRN.parquet",
  stage_args = list(
    imputation = list(k = 20L, n_pca_dims = 20L),
    transition = list(n_neighbors = 50L),
    grid = list(n_neighbors = 50L)
  )
)
CellOraclePlot(pancreas_sub, plot_type = "quiver")
} # }
